title: Horvitz-Thompson Risk Frontier under Neighborhood Seeding with Full-Neighborhood Exposure
banked_reason: Math and cited sources pass, but promised all-graph matched frontier remains open; delivered unmatched bracket is incremental below field floor (paper_score_ceiling 4.5 < 7.4), with no bounded faithful repair independently confirmed.
gap_reasons: The promised deliverable is a matched primitive all-graph frontier and resulting risk-ratio order, but this node expressly leaves that upper and frontier open and supplies only an unmatched finite bracket; the computable supporting results do not constitute the advertised theorem-level contribution.

The delivered bracket is Ω(d²/n) ≤ F(n,d) ≤ O(d min{1,d²/n}), leaving a growing multiplicative gap when both d and n/d grow, so sharp-risk-frontier and the exact precision-inflation order remain unresolved. The logarithmic row-sum obstruction disproves the proposed unweighted charging route but supplies neither a superquadratic spectral lower bound nor the missing quadratic operator upper; bipartite bounds and twin-broom calculations settle only special families. The remaining contribution is a narrow collection of seed-law witnesses and proof-route diagnostics, because covariance reduction and Rao–Blackwell contraction are elementary, and ordinary-versus-modified HT separation already appears under another law in [Kandiros et al., Theorem 4.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.10908v3). The TL;DR and justification contain no stale assertion that the frontier is established, but faithful writing cannot repair the unresolved central theorem, the benchmark's enumeration-only implementation, or the absence of a delivered rollout application, which constrain the projected paper score to 4.5. The classical Fourier identities are covered by [O'Donnell, Propositions 8.16 and 8.28](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.10386), while the [Li–Li slides](https://cdn.imsi.institute/videos/66451/oworKkEQQ9/slides.pdf) disclose an ongoing unrestricted-overlap analysis and do not establish a public archival collision. The inaccessible main theorem text of [Lu, Li, and Liu](https://academic.oup.com/jrsssb/advance-article-abstract/doi/10.1093/jrsssb/qkag077/8701320) requires source verification before any stronger noncollision claim, but that access limitation does not determine this below-floor assessment. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
Prove a universal quadratic-form bound xᵀK(G)x ≤ C(d+1)²‖x‖₂² over every admissible graph, with a numerical constant, completing the frontier using the existing star witnesses.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived lawful finite-(n,d) star lower bounds, a coarse all-graph upper bracket, the same-record Rao–Blackwell benchmark, and restricted-family/pivotal identities; the explicit logarithmic row-sum obstruction refuted the proposed unweighted proof route without refuting the quadratic spectral conjecture. After product-space sources were attested, math review passed, but the typed decision found kernel_substituted because the matched unrestricted upper and risk-ratio frontier remain open; normalized novelty is incremental (4.5 < 7.4), and independent D and main validity reviews found no bounded faithful repair. Formalization was not entered: no Lean proof, build, sorry/axiom audit, or accepted-tier certification is claimed; future fresh weighted-operator work is marked retry.
tldr: Universal invitation is observed locally only when an entire neighborhood receives treatment. For ordinary, unclipped exposure weighting under independent neighborhood-OR seeding, this note proves the exact covariance reduction, the all-\((n,d)\) lower bound \(F(n,d)\ge d(d+1)/(2n)\), and the finite upper bracket \(F(n,d)\le(4(d+1)-1)\min\{1,(1+d^2)/n\}\). It also proves that an estimator computable from the same treatment and factual-outcome record has risk of order \((d+1)/n\), so ordinary HT can be worse by an unbounded factor. Determining the matching unrestricted all-graph upper---and hence whether \(F(n,d)\asymp d^2/n\) and \(F(n,d)/B(n,d)\asymp d\)---remains Open-ended Question `oeq:sharp-risk-frontier`. The insurance application is prospective and would use the resolved frontier to assess universal-rollout precision.
gap: Li--Li printed slides 31--32 identify partial-overlap denominator compensation as unfinished. Public conflict-design operator bounds and randomized graph-cluster bounds use different assignment laws. No checked source supplies the unrestricted ordinary-HT frontier under the stipulated OR-seed law.
fill: The main open-ended question requires a primitive simultaneous population-size and degree scale, numerical constants, and matching legal graph and fixed-table witnesses. Endpoint reduction, binary stars, the original-record benchmark, and the bipartite interpolation are supporting results; the proposed contribution is the all-graph upper.
